text:
Maya: Heads-up — ACME (acct acme-prod) reporting a burst of 502/504s hitting Hosted API edge since 06:10 UTC. Spike started right after billing token rotation window. Customer says ~12-18% failures on generate streaming calls. sample req/ids below.

Sam: Escalation opened (INC-8492). Customer wants repro steps + ETA. They provided logs and a curl.

Maya: curl sample they sent:
```bash
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-rotated\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood/mini","input":"hello","stream":true}' \\n  https://api.run.redwood/v1/generate?stream=true
```

Maya: example request ids from their client: rq=rd-abc123, rd-def456, rd-ghi789. User-agent: acme-internal/2.4.1.

Alex: Noted. Any pattern by region or model? streaming vs non-streaming? Also did they rotate any SDKs?

Maya: Mostly streaming generate; a few embedding calls. Appears across us-east and eu-west nodes. Rotation was a billing key swap + auth cache flush triggered by our rotation job at 06:05 UTC.

ryan: I'm oncall. I'll pull edge traces and auth service traces for those req ids. Can someone drop a few raw log lines (edge) for one of the failing req ids?

Maya: Paste from edge logs (redacted):
```
[06:11:02.124] edge/us-east-1 envoy [upstream_reset] upstream reset before response, code: 502, req_id=rd-abc123, upstream: authz-svc-us-east, duration_ms=1500
[06:11:02.125] edge/us-east-1 envoy [upstream_response_timeout] response timeout 504, req_id=rd-def456, route: /v1/generate, client_id=acme-prod
```
zoe: Looks like authz upstream timeouts/connection resets surfacing as 502/504 at the gateway. Could be auth cache TTL/refresh storm post-rotation.

alex: Agree. If authz svc is slow or returning 5xx, envoy will show 502s. Can we check authz pod metrics around 06:05-06:15 (qps, errors, latency)?

ryan: Quick findings: authz service saw a 4x spike in calls, error rate jumped to 18% and p95 latency went from 60ms -> 1.2s during the rotation window. Heap of short-lived auth cache misses.

Maya: Customer confirms they retried and some calls succeeded once TTL stabilized. They hit us with heavy reconnects which probably amplified load.

zoe: Mitigation suggestions we should apply now: 1) temporarily increase auth cache TTL back to previous value, 2) apply request-level backoff on auth refreshes in rotation job, 3) enable a degraded-mode fallback for non-auth-critical paths (if available) to avoid edge-level fail-open.

alex: Agreed. Also add short-term route-level retry/backoff on edge to avoid immediate upstream pressure (careful not to amplify). I'll open a quick config patch to add 50ms jittered retry with circuit breaker on authz cluster.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by alex: edge-config/patch-authz-retry -> canary -> ok (deploy id: dpl-7423)

ryan: Rollout applied to canary nodes. Monitoring authz error rate now.

(10m later)

ryan: After canary patch + TTL bump, authz error rate down to 2%, envoy 502/504 rate for customer down to <1%. Customer message: "looks good from our side, failures dropped."

sam: Updated INC-8492 with mitigations and next-steps: permanent fix = make rotation job staggered and backoff-aware, increase auth cache capacity, add stricter circuit breaker and exponential backoff on the edge.

Maya: Customer satisfied, asked for postmortem. Assigning to eng-sre + eng-runtime to collaborate on root cause & permanent guardrails.

zoe: Action items: alex -> permanent edge retry/circuit change (RFC), ryan -> add authz autoscaling + cache metrics alerts, devex -> add runbook snippet for rotation window (how to avoid auth storm).

Maya: Thanks all. Closing loop with customer and scheduling postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
